title: Staying one step ahead of breast cancer, our talk with Europa Donna
content: Pink October is breast cancer awareness month. This year we had a chat with the Executive Director of the largest European breast cancer patient advocacy organisation. Find out what she said and learn more about what the EU is doing to support breast cancer prevention and care.

title: Winners of 2026 Megalizzi–Niedzielski prize for aspiring journalists announced
content: Yoana Kaloyanova (Bulgaria), Žan Tone Urbanija (Slovenia), and Marie Hartmann (Germany) have won the 2026 Megalizzi–Niedzielski prize for aspiring journalists. The prize honours the legacy of Antonio Megalizzi and Bartek Orent-Niedzielski, both killed in the 2018 terror attacks in Strasbourg.

title: 6 projects win prizes at 2026 EU REGIOSTARS awards
content: Six outstanding EU-funded projects, and the people behind them, have won prizes at the EU’s 2026 REGIOSTARS Awards. The awards recognise excellence in projects investing in regions, cities and communities. Winners included a battery recycling project in Germany and an AI holopresence in Slovakia.

title: AI adoption more than doubles in almost every EU strategic sector
content: According to a new EU analysis, the share of firms using AI in the EU’s 10 strategic sectors grew from 7% in 2021 to 18% in 2025. Media, energy and electronic sectors lead in AI adoption, while mobility, tourism and agri-food lag behind. This uneven growth is driven mainly by general-purpose AI.

title: Erasmus Days 2026: almost 11.000 events to take place across Europe
content: This week will see nearly 11.000 events take place across Europe and countries associated to the EU’s Erasmus+ programme during the 10th edition of the annual Erasmus Days. The 2026 theme ‘Learning and growing: skills for tomorrow' highlights the important role of Erasmus+ in skills development.

title: Programme for agile and rapid defence innovation gets green light
content: The new €115 million AGILE programme will provide rapid, agile and targeted financial support to small and medium-sized enterprises – including start-ups and scale-ups – to develop emerging and disruptive defence products. It complements the EU's existing toolbox of defence industrial instruments.

content: World Mental Health Day on October 10 serves as a reminder that good mental health is important and how we can prioritise it in our lives. At EU level, mental health is already a health priority. Find out more about what the EU is doing to ensure your mental wellbeing.

title: 46 new projects selected to help bolster EU’s supply of critical raw materials
content: Some 46 new strategic projects across the EU are set to bolster the EU’s supply of critical raw materials. They will help ensure that by 2030 EU capacity meets at least 10% of the EU’s annual consumption for extraction; 40% for processing and 25% for recycling of critical raw materials.

title: Updated rules to protect workers from exposure to dangerous chemicals
content: New rules will protect workers from exposure to harmful chemicals by setting new limit values for chemicals used in the battery, steel, chemical and textile industries. They also make clearer provisions for personal protective equipment. The measures should prevent around 1,700 lung cancer cases.

title: Preparing for a wider European Union
content: The Commission has adopted new measures on pre-enlargement policy reviews. The measures aim to ensure that the EU's governance, policies, and budget are ready for enlargement, while strengthening the protection of EU values and the rule of law.

title: Give your feedback on the proposed EU Kids Act
content: Provide your feedback by 26 November on the European Commission’s proposed EU Kids Act that aims to enhance the online safety of children across the EU. The Commission is seeking input from children, parents, guardians, teachers and educators, and online platforms covered by the proposal.

title: Returns to be made more effective
content: New rules aim to make returns more effective for people with no right to stay in the EU, introducing a European return order and opening the possibility of return hubs outside the EU. They complement the EU’s existing pact on migration and asylum and will aid its implementation.

title: €210 million boost to support over 700 researchers to build their careers in Europe
content: More than 700 additional researchers will be able to build their careers in Europe thanks to a boost of over €210 million to the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions – one of Europe's flagship programmes for research careers. The 2026 MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships received a record 21,627 applications.

title: Turning 18? Apply for a free DiscoverEU travel pass
content: The EU is offering DiscoverEU travel passes to 18-year-olds to explore Europe by train. Applications are open until 15 October 2026 at midday Brussels time. You can travel anytime between 1 March 2027 and 31 May 2028 for up to 7 days within a one-month period.

content: The Commission is gathering feedback on challenges and options for potential future measures to support the effective copyright protection amid market and technology developments. Among other issues, the targeted consultation focuses on the use of copyright-protected content in AI.

title: Commission proposes 5-point plan to strengthen security of EU external borders
content: The Commission has proposed a 5-point plan to prevent, anticipate and respond to sudden, mass illegal arrivals. Despite a resilient framework in place to manage migration, recent events have put the EU’s borders to the test. The plan will further strengthen the security of EU external borders.

title: Pharmaceutical industry reform increases patients’ access to medicine
content: New rules will increase patients’ access to medicine and make the EU’s pharmaceutical sector fairer and more competitive. The reform will allow fair access to affordable medicines and cut regulatory burdens on the pharmaceutical industry and strengthen security of supply to prevent shortages.

title: EU Screening Week: know your vital numbers
content: Know your numbers, protect your heart – take a simple check and join Europe’s fight against the silent killer. Today marks the start of the EU’s first-ever Screening Week that encourages people to get tested for cardiovascular diseases and raise awareness around prevention.

title: Celebrating the power of languages
content: The EU has 24 official and more than 60 regional or minority languages. On 26 September we celebrate the richness of our many languages and cultures on the European Day of Languages. title: EU and Canada secure almost €220 million in pledges for global ocean observation
content: Almost €220 million has been pledged at the launch of the OceanEye International Alliance for the Global Ocean Observing System in New York. The EU and 30 countries, including Canada, are members of the alliance. The funds will go towards reliable ocean observation around the world.

title: EU-led Team Gaza projects launched to restore essential services
content: The first flagship early recovery projects under the EU-led Team Gaza Initiative have been launched during the UN General Assembly High-Level Week in New York. The projects, worth a total of €43 million, will help restore essential water and solid waste management services for people in Gaza.

title: Making data centres energy efficient thanks to a new EU rating system
content: The rapid growth in data centres puts pressure on electricity grids and the use of natural resources, as well as contributes to increased carbon emissions. To limit these impacts, the European Commission has proposed a common rating scheme for data centres aimed at increasing energy transparency.

title: EU KIDS Act: helping children navigate a safer online world
content: In the face of growing concerns about the risks children and teenagers face when using online platforms, the EU has proposed a new KIDS Act. This will introduce a gradual uptake of social media for children in the EU, notably delaying access to social media until the age of 13.

title: €489 million proposed to help Portugal, Spain, Italy and Malta recover from severe storms
content: The European Commission has proposed to mobilise €489 million to help Portugal, Spain, Italy and Malta recover from severe storms and flooding in January and February 2026. The funding will support recovery operations to rebuild transport infrastructure and reestablish essential services.

title: Reform of EU customs code and e-commerce rules gets green light
content: The European Parliament has approved a major reform of the EU Customs Code that introduces stricter rules for e-commerce and establishes a new customs authority in Lille. By November 2026 a new handling fee for goods ordered directly from non-EU countries will come into effect.

title: State of the Union: “Europe has chosen to forge its own path”
content: In her 2026 State of the Union speech, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen shared the key priorities and flagship projects for the EU in the year to come. These include competitiveness and jobs, security and defence, climate resilience, social inclusion and democracy and rule of law.

title: Parliament proposes ways to bolster EU democracy against foreign interference
content: Members of the European Parliament have warned that foreign interference threats are an attack on the “very essence of the European project”, with citizens as primary victims. They adopted a report proposing practical recommendations on how the EU can do more to defend its democratic institutions.

title: Guaranteeing social rights for workers everywhere in the EU
content: The Commission has adopted proposals that will guarantee social rights for workers, regardless of where they choose to live in the EU. Workers will be able to have their professional skills understood everywhere in the EU and prove and claim their social security and health insurance rights.

title: Realising the potential of the EU’s outermost regions
content: A new Commission strategy will ensure that the EU’s outermost regions can fully realise their potential, with stronger support, greater resilience and fairer opportunities for their people. From Martinique to Madeira, the EU’s outermost regions play a key geostrategic role in today’s changing world.

title: New EU rules to help local authorities tackle the housing crisis
content: New EU rules have been proposed to support EU countries and cities address the affordable housing crisis, particularly housing used for purposes other than primary residence. The rules give public authorities the legal certainty when they choose to act, based on local specificities, within EU law.
